articles.title: Wedding checklist overview
articles.chat: A good plan is to work backwards from the wedding date. Book the venue, photographer, catering, and bridal dressing first, then invitations, seating, and the final guest count. I can walk you through it step by step.
questions: what should be on my wedding checklist
what should I do first on my wedding checklist
how does the wowwed checklist work
articles.answer: Work backwards from the wedding date. Book the scarce things first (venue, photographer, catering, bridal dressing), then invitations, fittings, seating, and final headcount. WowWed builds a Sri Lankan checklist from your ceremony type — open Wedding Checklist to tick items off by month and category.
points: 12 months out: budget, venue, auspicious date or church/kovil/mosque booking
6–10 months: photographer, catering, attire, theme, cake, entertainment
3–5 months: invitations, jewellery, contracts, fittings
1–2 months: seating chart, transport, final RSVPs, day-of timeline

articles.title: 12 months before
questions: what should I do 12 months before the wedding
what to do a year before
articles.answer: The first year is about locking the date, budget, and the places that book out.
points: Set a total budget and category splits on the Budget page
Confirm the wedding date (nekatha, church calendar, or mosque availability)
Book the venue or reception hall
Start a guest list so venue capacity and catering quotes are realistic
Hire photographer and videographer — popular names fill 9–12 months ahead

articles.title: 6 months before
questions: what should I do 6 months before the wedding
six month checklist
articles.answer: Around six months out, most vendors should be booked and the look of the day should be decided.
points: Book catering (rice and curry or hotel package) and the wedding cake
Book bridal dressing and the groom's national dress or suit
Choose theme, colours, and florist
Book band, DJ, or Kandyan dancers
Send save-the-date cards to family, especially outstation guests
Poruwa couples: book the Poruwa and ceremonial items

articles.title: 3 months before
questions: what should I do 3 months before the wedding
articles.answer: This is invitation, fitting, and contract season — still early enough to fix gaps.
points: Order and start delivering wedding invitations
Confirm vendor contracts and remaining deposits
Book hair, makeup, and clothing fittings
Order bridal jewellery if it is not already sorted
Collect RSVPs from close family first so catering numbers start to firm up

articles.title: 1 month before
questions: what should I do 1 month before the wedding
last month checklist
articles.answer: The last month is confirmation, not new booking. Lock numbers and the day-of plan.
points: Create the seating chart from confirmed guests
Arrange guest buses and parking
Confirm final headcount with the caterer
Create the wedding-day timeline
Confirm venue setup time and lighting
Pack an emergency kit (safety pins, stain stick, extra jewellery clasp, phone chargers)

articles.title: Wedding week
questions: what should I do in the wedding week
day-of checklist
articles.answer: Keep the week light. Confirm, rest, and hand the plan to someone who is not getting married.
points: Reconfirm every vendor's arrival time and contact person
Share the day-of timeline with the wedding crew
Prepare cash envelopes for remaining balances and tips
Steam outfits and pack ceremony items the night before
Assign one coordinator for vendor questions so the couple can stay present

articles.title: Poruwa ceremony checklist
questions: what is on a Poruwa checklist
Poruwa ceremony tasks
articles.answer: A Poruwa wedding adds ritual bookings on top of the shared WowWed checklist. Confirm the auspicious time early — it drives venue slot, photography, and catering.
points: Confirm auspicious date and nekatha with an astrologer
Book the Poruwa and ceremonial items (usually 6 months out)
Find Jayamangala Gatha singers and ashtaka reciters
Arrange kiribath and traditional sweetmeats
Plan the Magul homecoming
Collect Poruwa items the week before so nothing is missing on the day

articles.title: Church wedding checklist
questions: church wedding checklist
what to do for a church wedding
articles.answer: Church dates and paperwork take longer than a reception-only booking, so start with the parish.
points: Book the church and priest as early as 12 months ahead
Arrange the choir and hymn list
Prepare marriage certificate documents
Plan aisle flowers and church décor with parish rules in mind
Schedule the church rehearsal in the final month

articles.title: Hindu Tamil wedding checklist
questions: Hindu Tamil wedding checklist
kovil wedding tasks
articles.answer: Hindu Tamil weddings combine kovil ritual, thaali, and often a mehendi night — book the priest and hall together so muhurtham and catering line up.
points: Book the kovil and priest about 12 months out
Arrange the thaali / mangalsutra
Book the mehendi night
Arrange Hindu ceremonial items
Confirm vegetarian catering if the kovil or families require it

articles.title: Nikah ceremony checklist
questions: Nikah checklist
Muslim wedding tasks
articles.answer: A Nikah is often simpler than a large reception, but documents, mehr, and the walima still need a clear timeline.
points: Book the mosque and imam / qazi
Prepare nikah documents and agree the mehr
Plan the walima reception and guest count
Share dress-code notes with guests in advance

articles.title: Reception checklist
questions: reception only checklist
what to plan for the reception
articles.answer: A reception-only celebration still needs a host, a run of show, and a clear end time with the venue.
points: Book an MC for speeches and announcements
Plan cake cutting and first dance
Create the reception playlist with the band or DJ
Confirm last-song and venue close-down time

articles.title: Ceremony types in WowWed
questions: what ceremony types does WowWed support
which ceremonies can I plan
articles.answer: WowWed is built for Sri Lankan weddings. Pick a ceremony type in your wedding profile and the checklist plus vendor suggestions adapt to it.
points: Poruwa Ceremony — Sinhalese / Buddhist tradition
Church Wedding — Christian / Western tradition
Hindu Tamil Wedding — kovil and thaali rites
Muslim Nikah Ceremony — Islamic tradition
Reception — celebration only, or after a legal/religious ceremony elsewhere

articles.title: Choosing a ceremony type
questions: how do I choose a ceremony type
can I have two ceremonies
articles.answer: Choose the ceremony that families will actually attend as the 'main' event, then add a reception if you need a larger celebration. If you are having Poruwa in the morning and church or a hotel reception later, set the profile to the ritual that drives the checklist — usually Poruwa — and add reception tasks yourself.
points: One ritual + hotel reception is the most common split
Two full ceremonies need two timelines, two décor setups, and extra photography hours
Tell vendors the day's order so they quote the right package

articles.title: Poruwa ceremony
questions: how do I plan a Poruwa ceremony
what is a Poruwa ceremony
articles.answer: A Poruwa ceremony is the traditional Sinhalese Buddhist wedding ritual on a decorated wooden platform. The couple exchange vows with ashtaka recitations, Jayamangala Gatha, and symbolic offerings. Book the Poruwa, singers, and ritual items 3–6 months ahead, and lock nekatha before you confirm the venue slot.
points: Auspicious time (nekatha) comes first — photography and catering follow it
Allow extra time if a hotel reception is the same day
Brief the photographer on close-ups of the seven steps, rings, and family blessings

articles.title: Church wedding
questions: how do I plan a church wedding
what is a church wedding in Sri Lanka
articles.answer: A church wedding follows Christian liturgy — processional, readings, vows, and blessing. Parishes often require membership, documents, and a rehearsal. Décor is usually simpler than a hotel Poruwa; spend on music, flowers along the aisle, and a photographer who knows low light.
points: Ask the parish about photography rules and flash
Confirm whether rice-throwing or petals are allowed outside
Plan a buffer between church and reception for photos and travel

articles.title: Hindu Tamil wedding
questions: how do I plan a Hindu Tamil wedding
what happens at a Tamil wedding
articles.answer: A Hindu Tamil wedding centres on muhurtham, the thaali / mangalsutra, and priest-led rites at a kovil or hall. Families often host mehendi and a large vegetarian feast. Book priest, hall, and catering as one timeline so the ritual and meal are not rushed.
points: Confirm muhurtham before printing invitations
Jewellery and thaali need a dedicated pickup and security plan
Tell the photographer which moments cannot be missed (thaali tying, homam, blessings)

articles.title: Muslim Nikah ceremony
questions: how do I plan a Nikah
what is a Nikah ceremony
articles.answer: Nikah is the Islamic marriage contract, often at a mosque or home, followed by a walima reception. Keep the Nikah guest list closer and let the walima carry the larger celebration if you need it. Dress code, gender seating, and photography rules vary — ask the imam early and share notes with guests.
points: Documents and mehr should be agreed before invitations go out
A walima can be the same day or later — budget catering once per event
If seating is separated, plan that on the Seating Chart before the week of

articles.title: Reception
questions: how do I plan a reception-only wedding
what is a WowWed reception
articles.answer: Choose Reception when the legal or religious ceremony is separate (or already done) and WowWed is for the celebration. Focus on venue, catering, cake, MC, music, and seating. You can still add ritual tasks manually on the checklist if a short blessing is part of the evening.
points: Venue close-down time drives the run of show
An MC keeps cake cutting, speeches, and first dance on schedule
Guest count is the biggest cost lever — freeze RSVPs two weeks out

articles.title: Finding wedding vendors
questions: how do I choose and book wedding vendors
where do I find vendors
articles.answer: Browse WowWed Vendors by category and district, then send a booking request. Shortlist two options in each critical category so a decline does not stall the timeline. Filter by your district first — travel fees add up for photography, décor, and cake delivery.
points: Categories: Venue & Res. Halls, Bridal Service, Groom service, Photography & Videography, Jewellary, Floral & Déco, Caters, Cakes
Ask for a written package, overtime rate, and what is not included
Send booking requests early — peak months fill first

articles.title: Booking and negotiating
questions: how do vendor bookings work
should I pay a deposit
articles.answer: On WowWed you send a booking request; the vendor can accept, reject, or negotiate. Treat accept as a hold until the deposit and contract are in writing. Keep every change (guest count, overtime, extra hours) on paper.
points: Pay deposits only against a dated quotation
Record remaining balances in Budget so the week-of cash is planned
Confirm rain or power-cut backup for outdoor and garden venues

articles.title: Vendor contracts
questions: what should a vendor contract include
articles.answer: A useful contract is specific. Names, date, arrival time, guest count, package items, overtime, cancellation, and the remaining balance should all be written down.
points: Date, venue, and start/end times
Exact deliverables (hours of coverage, number of outfits, menu items)
Overtime rate and who authorises it
Cancellation and postponement terms
Final payment date — usually a few days before, not on the porch

articles.title: Venue & reception halls
articles.chat: {{ifGuests}}For {{guests}} guests, look for a hall that seats that number comfortably — not a huge ballroom that will look empty. {{/ifGuests}}{{ifBudget}}With {{budget}}, a mid-range hotel package or a well-chosen banquet hall is usually the right match. {{/ifBudget}}Visit at the same time of day as your ceremony, and ask what is included — chairs, Poruwa space, changing rooms, and a generator.
questions: how do I choose a wedding venue
venue booking tips
articles.answer: The venue sets guest capacity, catering style, and often the date. Visit in person at the same time of day as your ceremony. Ask what is included — chairs, Poruwa space, changing rooms, generator, and last-event time.
points: Match hall capacity to your realistic guest list, not the wish list
Colombo and Gampaha hotels book out first for December–January and July–August
Outdoor lawns need a rain plan and lighting, not just décor

articles.title: Photography & videography
questions: tips for booking a photographer
how to choose a wedding photographer
articles.answer: Book photography 9–12 months ahead for popular teams. Share your ceremony type so they know Poruwa close-ups, church low light, or thaali timing. A second shooter is worth it if you have two locations the same day.
points: Ask how many hours, how many cameras, and when the album is delivered
Pre-wedding shoots are usually a separate package
Confirm drone or church photography rules before the quote is signed

articles.title: Catering
questions: how do I book wedding catering
catering tips
articles.answer: Catering is usually the second-largest cost after the venue. Hotel packages bundle food with the hall; outside caterers need kitchen access, power, and a per-plate number locked two weeks before.
points: Get a tasting for the main menu, not only the cake
Plan welcome drinks, oil cakes, or sweetmeats as a separate line if they are not in the package
Vegetarian, halal, and children's plates should be counted, not guessed

articles.title: Bridal service
questions: how do I book bridal dressing
bridal service tips
articles.answer: Sri Lankan bridal service often includes Kandyan, Indian, or Western dressing plus hair and makeup. Book the dressing house when the date is firm, then schedule a trial and a fitting three months out.
points: Say whether you need a going-away outfit or homecoming saree
Trials should use the same jewellery and flowers as the day
Confirm who comes to the venue and at what time — overtime is common

articles.title: Groom service
questions: groom attire tips
how to book groom service
articles.answer: Groom service is easy to leave late — do not. National dress or a suit needs the same fitting window as the bride, especially if the party is matching.
points: Book 6–9 months out if the outfit is custom
Share colour cues with the bride's dressing house
Keep a spare shirt and comfortable shoes at the venue

articles.title: Jewellery
questions: when should I order bridal jewellery
jewellery tips
articles.answer: Order or reserve bridal jewellery about four months ahead so resizing and matching sets are not rushed. For Hindu weddings, treat the thaali as its own task with a trusted family member responsible on the day.
points: Insurance or a written custody plan for hired sets
Try jewellery at the makeup trial
Wedding rings are a separate, earlier purchase than the bridal set

articles.title: Floral & décor
questions: how do I book wedding flowers
décor tips
articles.answer: Florals and décor should follow the ceremony. A Poruwa needs traditional structure and jasmine; a church may limit attachments to pews; a hotel stage can take a larger flower wall. Book around six months out and share reference photos plus venue rules.
points: Ask what happens in heat — fresh flowers wilt in outdoor noon ceremonies
Lighting is part of décor, not an afterthought
Reuse ceremony flowers at the reception where the venue allows it

articles.title: Wedding cakes
questions: when should I order the wedding cake
cake vendor tips
articles.answer: Order the cake about six months ahead, with a tasting if the design is custom. Confirm delivery time, setup at the venue, and whether cutting service is included. A small display cake plus a sheet cake in the kitchen is a common cost saver for large guest counts.
points: Tell the baker the climate and how long the cake will sit out
Allergies and vegetarian icing should be on the order form
Transport is often extra — budget delivery, not only the cake

articles.title: Wedding budget basics
articles.chat: Tell me your total in rupees — or open Budget if you already set one — and I’ll split venue, catering, photography, décor, and a small buffer into actual amounts.
questions: how should I split my wedding budget
how do I start a wedding budget
articles.answer: Set a total first, then allocate by category, then track expenses against those envelopes.

articles.title: How to split the budget
articles.chat: {{ifBudget}}Based on {{budget}}, {{/ifBudget}}I can help you allocate expenses across the venue, catering, photography, decoration, and other services. A simple split is venue and food first, then photography, then attire and décor, with a little kept back for surprises.
questions: how do I allocate the wedding budget
budget percentages
articles.answer: Percentages are a starting point, not a rule. A hotel package that includes food will make 'venue' look huge and 'catering' small — that is fine if the total is still inside the cap. Adjust after the first two quotes.
points: If the hotel bundles hall + menu, treat it as one line and protect photography and attire next
Guest count moves catering more than it moves the photographer
Luxury décor is the category that quietly blows a 'standard' budget

articles.title: Venue share of the budget
questions: how much should the venue take from the budget
articles.answer: Plan 30–40% of the total for venue, or more if the hotel package includes catering. Get the minimum spend in writing — many halls charge for a floor even if your list shrinks. A smaller hall at a realistic headcount beats a grand ballroom at 60% capacity.

articles.title: Peak season pricing
questions: when is peak wedding season
does season change the cost
articles.answer: Sri Lankan peak months (roughly December–January and July–August) raise venue and photography prices and fill calendars. Auspicious weekends book first. If the date is flexible, a mid-week or off-peak date is one of the largest discounts you can get without cutting the guest list.
points: Ask vendors for weekday vs Saturday rates
Nekatha and church calendars still constrain 'any Saturday'
Cost prediction on the Budget page treats peak months as a higher factor

articles.title: Guest count and cost
questions: how does guest count affect budget
how many guests can I afford
articles.answer: Every extra guest is extra catering, cake, seating, and sometimes a larger hall. Build the guest list early, track RSVPs, and freeze the headcount about two weeks before for the caterer. A smaller confirmed list is cheaper than a padded 'maybe' list.
points: Use Guest List RSVP status so the seating chart and catering number match
Outstation guests may also need rooms and buses — log those as logistics, not catering
Children and crew meals should be counted if the caterer charges for them

articles.title: Deposits and cash flow
questions: when do I pay vendor deposits
how to plan wedding payments
articles.answer: Most vendors want a booking deposit now and the balance shortly before the wedding. Map those dates on the Budget page so three deposits do not land in the same month. Never pay a large balance in cash on the day without a receipt.
points: Typical split: 30–50% to book, remainder 1–2 weeks before
Keep a small cash float for day-of tips and overtime
If a vendor negotiates, get the new total in writing before the next payment

articles.title: Hidden costs
questions: what wedding costs do people forget
hidden wedding expenses
articles.answer: Quotes often omit the extras that appear in the last six weeks. Add a contingency line of 5–10% for them.
points: Service charge and VAT on hotel bills
Photography or décor overtime
Generator, corkage, and cake-cutting fees
Guest transport, welcome drinks, and printed extras
Alterations, extra makeup, and jewellery hire

articles.title: Ways to save
questions: how can I save money on the wedding
budget wedding tips
articles.answer: Cut the things guests will not notice before you cut photography hours or food quality. Date, guest count, and venue package are the three large levers.
points: Trim the guest list before you trim the menu
Reuse ceremony flowers at the reception
Display cake plus kitchen sheet cake for large lists
Weekday or off-peak dates
One strong photographer instead of two average packages

articles.title: AI cost prediction
questions: how does cost prediction work
can WowWed estimate my wedding cost
articles.answer: The Budget page estimates a total in LKR from Sri Lankan wedding records — guest count, district, ceremony, style (Budget / Standard / Premium), and season. Treat it as a planning range, then replace it with actual quotes.

articles.title: District and location costs
questions: does district change wedding cost
is Colombo more expensive
articles.answer: Yes. Colombo and nearby Gampaha usually cost more for halls, décor, and photography than Kurunegala, Matara, or Jaffna. Outstation weddings add vendor travel. Filter vendors by your district so quotes are comparable, and log travel as its own budget line if you hire a Colombo team for a hometown wedding.

articles.title: Track expenses
articles.answer: On Budget, set a total, add category envelopes (venue, catering, photos…), then log each payment as an expense. WowWed compares spent vs planned and flags when a category or the total is over. Open Expense overview for a cleaner list of what has gone out.
points: Add the category first, then the expense under it
Record deposits as soon as you pay them
If you go over, trim guest count or décor before cutting photography hours

articles.title: Guest list
articles.chat: {{ifGuests}}For {{guests}} guests, {{/ifGuests}}start with a clear list — family, friends, and anyone who must be there. Group people as you add them (bride’s family, groom’s family, friends). That makes seating and RSVPs much easier later.
articles.answer: Keep every name in Guest List — not in a side notebook. Add people one by one or import a CSV. Put each guest in a group (bride’s family, friends, VIP…). That group is what Smart Seating uses later, so it is worth doing now.
points: Name is required; phone or email helps you follow up
RSVP starts as Waiting until they reply
A realistic list is kinder to your venue and catering quotes

articles.title: Track RSVPs
articles.answer: Each guest has three replies: Coming, Waiting, or Not coming. Update them as answers arrive. Aim to lock the “Coming” number about two weeks before, then send that headcount to the caterer and build the seating chart from Coming guests only.
points: You can update several guests at once with bulk RSVP
Waiting guests still count toward invitations, not toward catering
Analytics shows how many have answered

articles.title: Import guests from CSV
articles.answer: On Guest List, download the CSV template, fill name, email, phone, group, rsvp, age, notes, and avoid, then import. Large family lists (hundreds of names) belong in a spreadsheet first. Duplicate names with the same phone or email are skipped so you can import more than once safely.
points: Keep the header row exactly as the template
Use Coming / Waiting / Not coming (or yes / no) for RSVP
Group names such as Bride's Family match WowWed’s groups

articles.title: Guest groups
articles.answer: Groups keep families together on the seating chart. Use Bride’s / Groom’s family and friends, colleagues, relatives, VIP, neighbours, or Other. VIP and close family usually sit nearer the couple. Mark people who should not sit together in the avoid note.

articles.title: Seating chart
articles.chat: I can help create a seating arrangement based on your guest relationships, table capacity, and seating constraints.{{ifGuests}} For {{guests}} guests, plan about {{tables}} — keep both families close to the couple, then seat friends together.{{/ifGuests}}
articles.answer: Add tables, then seat guests who are Coming. Start with family and VIP, then friends. You can place people by hand or run Smart Seating and fix anything that feels wrong. Only Coming guests should be seated — Waiting and Not coming stay off the floor plan.
points: Create tables before you auto-seat
Leave a couple of spare seats for late yes replies
Share the chart with family using the Seating PDF report

articles.title: Smart seating
articles.answer: Smart Seating groups Coming guests by their group (family, friends, VIP…) and fills tables without going over seat counts. It is a starting layout, not a final decision — drag anyone who should move. Run it again after RSVPs change.
points: Guests need a group on the Guest List for this to work well
Use Avoid notes for people who must not share a table
Check seating accuracy on Analytics after you auto-seat

articles.title: Tables
articles.answer: Add each table with a name, seat count, and shape (round, rectangle, square, head table, or standing). Suites such as family or VIP help you zone the room. A head table is usually for the couple and wedding crew; round tables of 8–10 work for most Sri Lankan halls.

articles.title: Invitations
articles.answer: Open Invitations, pick a template (Classic, Floral, Modern, or Poruwa), then fill your names, date, venue, and message. The preview updates as you type. Send save-the-dates earlier; send the full invitation about 6–8 weeks before, once the venue and time are firm.
points: Your wedding profile names and date can fill the card for you
Keep one clear RSVP instruction (phone, WhatsApp, or WowWed list)
Print extras for elders who prefer a paper card

articles.title: Download invitations
articles.answer: When the design looks right, export or print from the Invitations studio. Use PDF for the printer and for WhatsApp sharing. Double-check spelling of both families’ names before you send a hundred copies.

articles.title: Wedding crew
articles.answer: Wedding Crew is your bridesmaids, groomsmen, best man, maid of honour, flower girl, ring bearer, and day-of helpers. Add each person and a role so you know who to call when a vendor arrives. Give one coordinator the day-of timeline — it should not be the couple.

articles.title: Analytics
articles.answer: Analytics is a snapshot of your own wedding — RSVP split, checklist progress, budget used, seating quality, and readiness score. Nothing here is shared with other couples. Use it when you want to see what still needs attention this week.

articles.title: PDF reports
articles.answer: Reports can print five PDFs: guest list, budget, vendors, seating, or a full summary. Use them when a parent or vendor asks “send me the list”. Each report uses the data already in your dashboard — update RSVPs or expenses first, then download.

articles.title: Readiness score
articles.answer: Your dashboard readiness score is the equal average of checklist progress, RSVP confirmations, and budget health (a set budget that stays on track — not merely how much you have spent). Green means you are on track, yellow means some gaps, red means key pieces are missing. Tick checklist items, collect RSVPs, and keep the budget on plan to lift the score — it is a reminder, not a grade.

articles.title: Wedding profile
articles.answer: Tap the couple names in the sidebar (or Settings) to edit partners’ names, ceremony type, district, date, and guest count. Ceremony type rebuilds suggested checklist tasks, and district helps vendor search and cost prediction. Change these early so the rest of WowWed stays in sync.

articles.title: How to use WowWed
articles.chat: Start on Home for the countdown and Readiness Score. Fill your wedding profile first — names, date, ceremony (Poruwa, church, Hindu, or Nikah), and district — so the Sri Lankan checklist, vendor match, and cost prediction line up. Then guests, seating, invitations, budget in LKR, and vendors.
articles.answer: Start on Home for the countdown and readiness score. Work left to right: Checklist, Guests, Seating, Invitations, Budget, Vendors. Analytics and Reports are for checking progress. This assistant stays on your device and only answers from the rules in this knowledge base.
points: Fill the wedding profile first (date, ceremony, district)
Import or type the guest list before seating
Send vendor booking requests from Vendors, then log deposits in Budget

articles.title: Vendor match
articles.answer: On Vendors, tap Match. WowWed shortlists listings that fit your district, budget, and ceremony using rules — not ML. Always read the package and send a booking request to confirm the date.

articles.title: Wedding ideas
articles.answer: Couples usually start with four choices: theme, colours, setting (indoor / garden / beach), and food style. Pick those first — they guide the Poruwa or church décor, invitations, and outfits. Tap Ideas & style for ready-made questions, or type “wedding theme”, “colour palette”, or “decoration ideas”.
points: Theme — traditional gold & ivory, garden green, beach coral, or modern minimal
Colours — two mains + one accent, tested in hall lighting
Setting — indoor hall, hotel garden, or coast, with a rain plan
Food — rice-and-curry, hotel buffet, or live hopper / kottu stations
articles.routeLabel: Add style tasks to the checklist

articles.title: Wedding theme ideas
articles.answer: A theme is a simple story, not a costume party. Choose one that fits your ceremony and venue, then repeat it in flowers, lighting, and the invitation. Popular Sri Lankan directions couples search for:
points: Classic Kandyan — carved Poruwa, ivory, gold, jasmine, brass lamps
Garden romance — whites, greens, hanging florals, fairy lights
Beach / south-coast — sand, coral, light blue, coconut and lotus details
Hill-country — emerald, champagne, tea-estate views, wood and ferns
Modern minimal — ivory, soft peach, clean stage, fewer heavy backdrops
Jewel fusion — burgundy or emerald with gold for a night hotel reception

articles.title: Colour palette ideas
articles.answer: Pick two main colours and one accent, then use them on the Poruwa or aisle, table flowers, and bridesmaid outfits. Match the venue: gold halls like maroon and ivory; gardens like sage and cream; beaches like coral and sand.
points: Sinhala / Poruwa — red, gold, and white for prosperity and the Kandyan saree
Hindu Tamil — bright red, yellow, and green with temple flowers
Nikah / walima — jewel blues, greens, purples, or soft pastels
Church — ivory, blush, and greenery (check parish décor rules)
2025–26 trend — ivory + soft gold + burnt orange, or emerald + burgundy
articles.routeLabel: Add colour choices to your tasks

articles.title: Decoration ideas
articles.answer: Spend on what the camera and guests see first: ceremony backdrop, entrance, and the couple’s table. Keep the Poruwa or altar readable — too many flowers hide the ritual. Reuse ceremony flowers at the reception if the venue allows it.
points: Poruwa: carved wood, jasmine, lotus, punkala pots, oil lamps — or a simple ivory floral arch
Entrance: name board, drapes, and a photo wall guests actually use
Tables: low centrepieces so people can talk; candles or fairy lights after dark
Stage: one strong backdrop beats five competing props
Heat tip: outdoor noon flowers wilt — plan shade or indoor backup

articles.title: Bridal look ideas
articles.answer: Sri Lankan brides often wear a Kandyan osariya or Indian saree for the ritual and change for the reception. A Western gown works for church or a hotel evening. Book the dressing house when the date is firm, then trial hair, makeup, and jewellery together.
points: Poruwa day: Kandyan saree in white, gold, or cream
Hindu wedding: Kanchipuram or bright silk, with thaali planned as its own task
Church: gown or modest saree — ask the parish about veil and shoulders
Homecoming: a red or bright saree is still the usual “second look”
Keep one going-away outfit if you have photos after the reception

articles.title: Bridesmaid ideas
articles.answer: Give the party one colour family, not identical factory dresses. Jewel emerald, burgundy, or champagne photographs well in Sri Lankan halls. Groomsmen can echo the same colour in the pocket square or sash so the group looks planned, not uniform.

articles.title: Food and menu ideas
articles.answer: Guests remember food more than napkin folds. A hotel package is simplest. If you want a “Sri Lankan Google favourite” menu, mix a main buffet with one or two live stations — hoppers, kottu, or a seafood grill — plus traditional sweets.
points: Welcome: iced drinks, oil cakes, kevum, or a short-eats table
Main: rice and curry, hotel international buffet, or both
Live corners: hoppers, kottu, string hoppers, or a dessert watalappan station
Count vegetarian, halal, and children’s plates — do not guess
Lock the headcount two weeks out with the caterer

articles.title: Cake ideas
articles.answer: A small display cake for photos plus a kitchen sheet cake is the usual way to feed a large Sri Lankan guest list without paying for a five-tier sculpture. Chocolate, butter cake, and fruit cake travel well in heat; cream-heavy designs need air-conditioning.

articles.title: Wedding favours
articles.answer: Skip plastic trinkets guests leave on the table. Better return-gifts: seed packets, local tea, jaggery sweets, handmade soap, or a small plant. One nice thing beats five cheap things. Put a simple thank-you note with your names and date.

articles.title: Music and first dance
articles.answer: Build three playlists: ceremony (soft, no lyrics that clash with ritual), dinner (talkable volume), and dance (the late energy). For Poruwa, Jayamangala Gatha is the musical heart — do not bury it under a DJ. A live Kandyan drum or violin moment photographs well. First dance: pick a song you both already know, 2–3 minutes, then invite parents in.

articles.title: Honeymoon ideas
articles.answer: Many couples stay in Sri Lanka for 3–5 nights before a later overseas trip: south-coast beach (Mirissa, Bentota), hill country (Ella, Nuwara Eliya), or a quiet Galle Fort hotel. Book refundable rooms until vendor balances are paid. Passports and leave from work need more lead time than the hotel.

articles.title: Rain and backup plans
articles.answer: Southwest monsoon (May–September) and northeast rains can still appear on a “dry” weekend. If any part is outdoor, write a Plan B in the venue contract: indoor hall, tent, or covered porch, plus where the Poruwa moves. Lighting and a generator matter as much as the tent.
points: Ask the hotel what happens if rain starts at nekatha time
Keep a clear umbrella pair for photos — it looks intentional
Tell the photographer and florist the backup location in advance

articles.title: Vows and speeches
articles.answer: Keep vows short (45–90 seconds) and specific — one memory, one promise, one laugh. Speeches: welcome, parents or siblings, best man / maid of honour, couple last. Give speakers a time limit (3 minutes) and a microphone test. For Poruwa, the ashtaka and blessings already carry the ritual — extra speeches belong at the reception.
articles.routeLabel: Assign speech roles in Wedding Crew

articles.title: Photo ideas
articles.answer: Give the photographer a short must-have list so they are not guessing: couple portraits, both families, Poruwa or altar details, thaali or rings, cake, and grandparents. Golden hour outside beats a dark hall. A second shooter helps if church and hotel are on the same day.
points: Poruwa: seven steps, close-ups of hands, lamps, and family blessings
Church: aisle walk, vows, signing — check flash rules
Hindu: thaali tying and homam cannot be missed
Reception: entrance, first dance, cake, and a 20-minute couple break for portraits

articles.title: Guest dress code
articles.answer: Put the dress code on the invitation: “National or formal”, “Garden — heels will sink”, or “Mosque — covered shoulders”. Suggest a colour to avoid if it clashes with the bridal party (often white or the exact bridesmaid shade). For Nikah, share modest-dress notes early.

articles.title: Homecoming
articles.answer: The Magul homecoming is often the next day at the groom’s home: a shorter blessing, kiribath, sweets, and a bright saree for the bride. Treat it as a second mini-event — guest list, food, and a photographer hour — not an afterthought. Put it on the checklist so it has a budget line.

articles.title: Pre-wedding events
articles.answer: You do not need every party. Pick one or two: engagement, mehendi, bachelor/hen night, or a small home blessing. Each extra event is another outfit, another caterer, and another day off work. Hindu weddings often include mehendi; many Sinhala couples keep only the wedding day plus homecoming.

articles.title: Indoor, garden, or beach
articles.answer: Indoor hotel halls are safest for large lists, nekatha timing, and rain. You get rooms, generators, and a kitchen — at a higher package price. Outdoor lawns and gardens look beautiful and need shade, insects, lighting, a rain cover, and extra décor. Beach weddings (Galle, Bentota, Mirissa) are windy — weight the décor and keep the ceremony short. Mixed (Poruwa indoor, photos in the garden) is the usual Sri Lankan compromise.

articles.title: Who pays
articles.answer: There is no single Sri Lankan rule anymore. Talk early: some families still host the home ceremony while the couple pays the hotel; others split 50/50; some couples pay all of it. Write the agreement down so vendor deposits do not surprise anyone. Use WowWed Budget so every contribution is visible.

articles.title: Wedding-day timeline
articles.answer: Work backwards from nekatha, church time, or the hotel slot. Hair and dressing take longer than you think. Photography usually starts at getting-ready, not at the ceremony. Put a 30–45 minute buffer between ceremony and reception for photos and travel. Give one coordinator (not the couple) the printed timeline and vendor numbers.
points: Getting ready and family photos — start photography here
Ceremony (Poruwa / church / kovil / nikah) is often 45–90 minutes; a full Poruwa can run longer
Couple + family portraits after the ritual
Reception: entrance, dinner, speeches, cake, first dance, send-off
Send invitations about 6–8 weeks before; confirm vendors 2–4 weeks before; freeze the guest list about 2 weeks before catering

articles.title: Wedding cost in Sri Lanka
articles.answer: There is no single price. Hometown and outstation weddings are usually cheaper than Colombo hotel packages. Guest count, season, and whether food is bundled with the hall move the total more than the cake or favours.
points: Small / hometown (about 80–120 guests): often around Rs. 0.8–1.5 million
Mid-range hotel (about 150–200 guests): often Rs. 2–4 million
Premium Colombo weekend: Rs. 4 million and up
Keep 5–10% extra for VAT, overtime, and last-minute extras

articles.title: Rs. 1 million budget
articles.chat: Rs. 1 million can work if you keep the guest list smaller and skip a luxury hotel package. Prioritise food, a good photographer, and a venue that already includes chairs and a kitchen.
articles.answer: Rs. 1 million is a tight but possible Sri Lankan wedding if you keep the list small and skip a luxury hotel package. Prioritise food, a decent photographer, and a venue that already includes chairs and a kitchen.
points: Aim for about 80–120 guests, not 200
Hometown hall, home garden, or a modest hotel weekday package
One photographer (skip a second shooter and a long film)
Simple Poruwa or ceremony décor; reuse flowers at the reception
Family catering or a set menu instead of a live-station buffet

articles.title: Rs. 2 million budget
articles.chat: Based on your budget of Rs. 2 million, I can help you allocate expenses across the venue, catering, photography, decoration, and other services.{{ifGuests}} For {{guests}} guests, venue and food will take the largest share.{{/ifGuests}}
articles.answer: Rs. 2 million usually covers a mid-range wedding of about 120–180 guests if you watch the hall package. Allocate the largest slices to venue + catering, then photography, then attire.
points: Venue + food: about Rs. 1.0–1.3 million
Photography & video: about Rs. 200,000–350,000
Attire, makeup, and jewellery hire: about Rs. 150,000–250,000
Décor, cake, music, invitations, and extras share the rest
Hold about Rs. 100,000–200,000 as contingency

articles.title: Catering share of the budget
articles.answer: Plan about 20–25% of the total for catering, or more if the hotel bill is mostly food. Per-plate cost times guest count is the real number — shrinking the list saves more than swapping dessert.

articles.title: Photography share of the budget
articles.answer: Plan about 10–15% for photography and videography. This is the memory you cannot restage. If the budget is tight, keep a strong photographer and shorten hours or skip the cinematic film before you hire a cheap unknown team.

articles.title: Decoration share of the budget
articles.answer: Décor often lands around 8–12% unless you want a full stage and floral ceiling. Spend on the ceremony backdrop and the couple’s table first. Luxury décor is the category that most often blows a ‘standard’ budget.

articles.title: Wedding dress / saree share
articles.answer: Attire and jewellery together are often 8–12% of the total. A Kandyan or Indian bridal hire is usually cheaper than a custom gown. Budget the trial, extra makeup, and a going-away or homecoming outfit separately so they do not surprise you.

articles.title: Groom outfit share
articles.answer: The groom’s outfit is usually a smaller line than the bride’s — still book fittings early. National dress or a hired suit plus shoes and grooming often sits well below 5% of a mid-range budget. Match colours with the bridal house so photos look planned.

articles.title: Most expensive wedding services
articles.answer: In Sri Lanka the large costs are almost always venue (especially a Colombo hotel package), catering, and then photography. Décor can overtake photography if you request a full floral stage. Cake, invitations, and favours are small compared with guest count.
points: Protect venue + food first — they serve every guest
Protect photography second — you cannot redo the day
Cut décor scale, peak-season dates, and extra guests before you cut food quality

articles.title: Photography vs decoration
articles.answer: If you must choose, spend more on photography. Guests remember the food and the pictures; heavy décor is forgotten after the hall lights come on. Keep décor focused on the ceremony backdrop and head table, and put the rest of that money into a second shooter or more coverage hours.

articles.title: Venue for about 100 guests
articles.answer: For about 100 guests, a hotel banquet room, a boutique villa, a home garden with a hired marquee, or a small restaurant hall all work. Avoid a 400-seat ballroom — it will look empty and you may still pay a high minimum spend. Confirm seated capacity, not standing cocktail numbers.

articles.title: Venue for about 200 guests
articles.answer: For about 200 guests you usually need a hotel ballroom, a large banquet hall, or a well-planned outdoor space with backup cover. Check kitchen capacity, parking, generator, and how many round tables of 8–10 actually fit. A packed 150-seat room is worse than a slightly larger hall.

articles.title: Questions to ask a venue
articles.answer: Visit at the same time of day as your ceremony and get the answers in writing before you pay a deposit.
points: What is included — chairs, Poruwa space, changing rooms, air-con, generator?
What is the minimum spend and the last-event / music cut-off time?
Can we bring an outside caterer, florist, or photographer?
What are corkage, cake-cutting, and overtime fees?
Is there a rain plan for lawns, and where do guests park?

articles.title: When to book the venue
articles.answer: Book the venue first, usually 9–12 months ahead (12–18 months for popular Colombo Saturday halls in December–January). The date and guest capacity unlock catering, photography, and invitations. Do not print cards until the hall has confirmed the slot in writing.

articles.title: Choosing a wedding planner
articles.answer: A planner is worth it if you have two ceremonies, a large list, or little time. Ask what is included (vendor talks, day-of coordination, or full planning), how many weddings they run the same weekend, and whether they take commission from vendors. For a smaller wedding, a trusted family coordinator plus WowWed checklists may be enough.

articles.title: Choosing a DJ or music
articles.answer: Listen to a live or recorded set, not only photos. Share a must-play and do-not-play list, confirm they have backup speakers, and check hotel volume rules. A good DJ who reads the room beats an expensive band that only plays for 45 minutes.

articles.title: Questions to ask a vendor
articles.answer: Compare at least two quotes with the same date, guest count, and hours. Before you hire anyone, check the contract, not only the Instagram page.
points: What is included, and what costs extra (overtime, travel, extra albums)?
Have they worked your ceremony type and this venue before?
When is the deposit, the balance, and the cancellation rule?
Who actually turns up on the day — the person you met, or a junior?
Can you see a full wedding (not only highlights) from a similar budget?

articles.title: Reducing the guest list
articles.answer: A smaller list is the fastest way to protect food, hall, and seating costs. Start with people you would miss if they were not there, then household units (not every cousin by name), then colleagues. Drop plus-ones you have never met, and skip distant relatives you would not invite to dinner.

articles.title: If a guest does not RSVP
articles.answer: Do not guess. Call or WhatsApp once, then again a week later. Elders often reply only by phone. If there is still no answer about two weeks before, mark them Not coming for catering, leave one spare seat if they are close family, and tell the caterer a firm number. Waiting forever is how buffets run short.

articles.title: Guest count on Rs. 1 million
articles.answer: On Rs. 1 million, plan for about 80–120 guests unless family is cooking at home. Every extra person is extra food, cake, and sometimes a larger hall. Build the list in WowWed, track RSVPs, and freeze the number before you pay the catering balance.

articles.title: Where families and friends sit
articles.answer: Seat the couple at the head table. Put the bride’s parents and closest relatives at the nearest tables on her side, and the groom’s family on his side — that is the usual Sri Lankan pattern. VIP and grandparents closer than distant cousins. Friends can mix at mid-room tables; keep school and office groups together so nobody sits among strangers.

articles.title: Guests who cannot sit together
articles.answer: On the Guest List, put an Avoid note on anyone who must not share a table (divorced relatives, rival uncles, ex-partners). Smart Seating uses that note. If you seat by hand, place those guests on opposite sides of the room with a buffer table, and do not put them in the same suite.

articles.title: Seating for 100 guests
articles.answer: For 100 seated guests, plan about 10–12 round tables of 8–10, plus a head table. Add two spare seats for late yes replies. Create tables in Seating Chart first, mark Coming guests only, then run Smart Seating and fix family placement by hand.

articles.title: Sri Lankan wedding traditions
articles.chat: I can help you plan a traditional Sri Lankan wedding, including the Poruwa ceremony, vendors, budget, and schedule. The Poruwa, an auspicious time, and elders’ blessings are the heart of it — then the reception can be as simple or as grand as you like.
articles.answer: A traditional Sinhala wedding centres on the Poruwa (the decorated wooden platform), an auspicious nekatha time, Jayamangala Gatha, and elders’ blessings. Many couples also have a church, Hindu, or Nikah ceremony, then a hotel reception. Homecoming (magul) the next day is still common. Tell WowWed your ceremony type so checklists and vendors match.
points: Poruwa, ashtaka, and traditional items if you follow Sinhala custom
Family jewellery, betel, and oil lamps as elders expect
Hotel or home reception after the ritual
Vendors: venue, caterer, photographer, florist/Poruwa décor, bridal dressing, music

articles.title: Poruwa ceremony costs
articles.answer: A Poruwa budget is usually the structure, floral décor, ashtaka reciter, Jayamangala singers, traditional trays, and sometimes a specialist coordinator. Simple hometown setups may be tens of thousands of rupees; a fully decorated hotel Poruwa with heavy florals can run into a few hundred thousand. Ask what the florist includes — the wooden Poruwa hire is often separate from flowers.

articles.title: Traditional wedding on a low budget
articles.answer: Keep the ritual, cut the scale. A home or temple Poruwa with family flowers, a hired simple structure, and a rice-and-curry lunch for a short list looks more ‘Sri Lankan’ than a half-empty ballroom. Spend on the photographer and the meal; print fewer programmes and skip a giant stage.

articles.title: Traditional or modern
articles.chat: I can help you plan a traditional Sri Lankan wedding, including the Poruwa ceremony, vendors, budget, and schedule — or a more modern reception if you prefer both. Many couples keep the ritual traditional and let the evening feel contemporary.
articles.answer: Choose the ritual your families need, then modernise the party if you want. A traditional Sri Lankan wedding keeps Poruwa or kovil/nikah customs, national dress, and elder-led seating. A modern one may use a short civil or hotel ceremony, a lighter colour palette, and a playlist-led reception. Many couples do both: traditional morning, modern evening. Pick based on family expectation, guest count, and budget — not on Pinterest alone.

articles.title: Small or large wedding
articles.answer: A small wedding (often under 100 guests) is easier on budget, seating, and nerves — think villa, garden, or a weekday hotel suite. A large wedding (200+) needs a hall with real capacity, more ushers, earlier RSVPs, and a tighter timeline. Guest count should follow budget and venue, not the other way around.

articles.title: Low-budget wedding theme
articles.answer: Pick a simple story you can repeat with lighting and greenery, not with imported flowers. Strong low-cost directions: ivory + greenery garden, classic white Poruwa with jasmine, or modern minimal (candles, drapes, one backdrop). Avoid multiple themes in one hall. Reuse ceremony flowers at the reception.

articles.title: Which option is best
articles.answer: The ‘best’ vendor is the one that fits your date, district, guest count, and remaining budget — not the most followers. Compare two quotes with the same hours and inclusions. Value usually means: reliable team, clear contract, and work that matches your ceremony, not the cheapest line. If money is short, protect venue, food, and photography; trim décor and extras.
